_comment: Allow rules must live here rather than in settings.json: a project settings.json's allow rules are ignored until the workspace is trusted, and under `--permission-mode dontAsk` that denies every call, so a scheduled run fails having written nothing - the same way every time, quietly. Local settings need no trust.
_comment_shell: Bash and PowerShell are allowed broadly on purpose. The constraint is not the permission rule but .claude/hooks/guard_commands.py, which allowlists exactly two of this bot's own scripts and denies everything else - including npm install, pip, git and every network fetch tool. Hooks apply regardless of trust and cannot be bypassed by the model; a permission-rule prefix list over shell strings can be.
_comment_read: Read is Agency-wide because diagnosis needs it: you cannot fix the control plane without reading the bots it reports on. The secrets are carved back out by deny rules in settings.json, which beat these.
_comment_fetch: WebFetch is domain-locked; WebSearch is not, because search returns text and fetching is the boundary that matters. docs.claude.com is here because the root CLAUDE.md requires the settings/hook schema to be confirmed against the docs rather than recalled.
